statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-113425 is a use after free in the nginx mail proxy module that a remote unauthenticated client can trigger when nginx is configured as a mail proxy. nginx.org lists 0.5.33 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 (https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html, https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163931, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113425). Every nginx-mainline package published for Alpine 3.23 (1.28.2-r0 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r7, on x86_64 and aarch64, except 1.29.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only) contains no files and only depends on the nginx package of the same version. The mail proxy code ships in that source's separate nginx-mod-mail package, not in nginx-mainline or in the nginx binary. Pending: whether this owner should be recorded as not containing the component, or should follow the nginx owner it depends on, which is affected.

CVE-2026-113425 is a use after free in the nginx mail proxy module that a remote unauthenticated client can trigger when nginx is configured as a mail proxy. nginx.org lists 0.5.33 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 (https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html, https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163931, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113425). For Alpine 3.24, 1.31.9-r5 is the first and only nginx-mainline build of 1.31.9; its nginx binary reports nginx/1.31.9 on x86_64 and aarch64 and its nginx-mainline-mod-mail package carries the fixed module. The builds 1.31.2-r2 to 1.31.8-r5 ship the mail module from upstream releases in the vulnerable range with no backport, and the earlier 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 packages contain no files and depend on the vulnerable nginx package of the same version. The 1.31.2 to 1.31.8 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable, so the range ends at 1.31.9-r5.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-113425 is a use after free in the nginx mail proxy module that a remote unauthenticated client can trigger when nginx is configured as a mail proxy. nginx.org lists 0.5.33 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 (https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html, https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163931, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113425). Every nginx build published for Alpine 3.23 (1.28.0-r8 to 1.28.3-r9 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r7) is an upstream release in the vulnerable range, and its nginx-mod-mail package ships the mail module; on x86_64, 1.28.3-r4 and 1.29.7-r0 publish no nginx-mod-mail package. Alpine backported the fix in its 1.28.3-r8 package (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/nginx/APKBUILD). The newest builds here, 1.28.3-r9 and 1.29.8-r7, were built on 2026-08-03, before Alpine added that backport on 2026-11-19, and none of the builds carries it. No fixed build is published for this owner yet.

Every nginx build published for Alpine 3.24 (1.28.3-r0 on aarch64 only, 1.28.3-r1, 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.30.3-r1, 1.30.3-r2, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1) is an upstream release in the vulnerable range, ships the mail module in its nginx-mod-mail package, and carries no backport of the fix. The 1.31.2 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable. No fixed build is published for this owner yet.

CVE-2026-113425 is a use after free in the nginx mail proxy module that a remote unauthenticated client can trigger when nginx is configured as a mail proxy. nginx.org lists 0.5.33 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 (https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html, https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163931, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113425). Debian fixed it for trixie in nginx 1.26.3-3+deb13u11 (DSA-6642-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-113425), backporting the five upstream mail fixes the tracker lists, starting with https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/9e811a43119ac902f0d0296fb4afb34bb063cf1b. Every nginx build of this owner is a rebuild of a Debian 1.26.3-3+deb13u trixie revision, and the mail module, ngx_mail_module.so, ships in its libnginx-mod-mail package. The DHI Debian repository currently holds four builds: two rebuilds of 1.26.3-3+deb13u9 and one each of 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 and 1.26.3-3+deb13u11. We checked the libnginx-mod-mail and libnginx-mod-mail-dbgsym packages of all four on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums. Only the 1.26.3-3+deb13u11 rebuild has the functions the fix adds in the module's debug symbols (ngx_mail_block_read, ngx_mail_auth_http_block_write, ngx_mail_proxy_block_write and ngx_mail_smtp_block_writing), and only its Debian changelog lists the CVE-2026-113425 patch; every build has the pre-existing ngx_mail_proxy_block_read, which serves as the control. All earlier rebuilds sort below it, so the range ends at the first rebuild of 1.26.3-3+deb13u11.
